title: Stare at the Dot on This Blue Banana #illusion #science
description:
Stare at the dot on the blue banana for about 10 seconds, keep your eyes still, then look at the white screen. Most people see a faint yellow banana, but nothing on your screen is yellow. Staring wore down the cells in your eyes that sense blue. On white, the blue signal is weak, so yellow wins. This is a negative afterimage. Didn't see it? Stare a little longer and try again.

More on how your eyes fill in what isn't there: Why don't you see the hole in your vision? https://youtu.be/i4d-ZYG2Ttc

Sources
- Illusions Index, Negative afterimages (illusionsindex.org/i/negative-afterimages)
- BrainFacts.org, Aftereffects (brainfacts.org, 2018)
- Wolfe et al., Sensation & Perception: afterimages and opponent colour (learninglink.oup.com)
- The cell-signal bars in the animation are schematic; part of the effect happens in the brain's colour channels

Try it: how many seconds did you need to see yellow?

Script, voice and animation are AI-produced (Claude; Kokoro voice). Every claim is checked against the sources above.
